result.title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents
result.summary: Personal-agent memory has largely focused on learning what users know, prefer, and want. However, knowing the user does not necessarily mean knowing what the user and the agent have established together. An assistant's proposal should not become an authorized instruction merely because it is remembered. We introduce Grounding Awareness, the ability to distinguish accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements when selecting actions. We develop a controlled benchmark to test whether agents can tell the difference between proposals users have accepted and those they have not, and whether they apply accepted arrangements only where appropriate. Across multiple agents and memory systems, we find that strong memory performance does not ensure Grounding Awareness. More surprisingly, providing more complete user information can increase execution of unacknowledged proposals, while persistent memory can cause agents to treat these proposals as if they were user instructions. We trace these failures through memory writing, retrieval, and action selection. Finally, we introduce Grounding Layer, a lightweight, training-free extension that explicitly tracks grounding status and checks consequential actions, substantially improving agent behavior without modifying models or memory systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「Grounding Awareness」，即个人智能体能否区分用户已接受、未获确认、被修改和限定范围的安排，并构建受控基准测试多种智能体与记忆系统；结果显示强记忆性能并不保证该能力，给出更完整的用户信息反而增加执行未确认提议，且持久记忆会让智能体把提议当作指令。作者进一步提出免训练的 Grounding Layer，显式跟踪 grounding 状态并在有后果的动作前核查。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作关于「已确立状态 vs 仅被提出的内容」的区分与行动前核查，可能与 LVR 中 latent 假设或视觉证据的来源归属、以及是否真被用于作答的核查问题相通，其免训练状态跟踪与门控做法可供核查借鉴。
